luma_limited_u8 — IMGMETRICS iqa op

• Data kinds: any → any

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.luma_limited_u8(rgb) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import iqatid; iqatid.luma_limited_u8(rgb) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsimgmetrics.get("luma_limited_u8"))

Usage

RGB (H, W, 3) uint8 → uint8 (H, W) of Y′ = round(16 + (65.481 R + 128.553 G + 24.966 B) / 255).

Luminance in ITU-R BT.601 limited range (studio swing). Black (0,0,0) → 16, white (255,255,255) → 235. Compared with full range Y = 0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B (black 0, white 255) it is a different quantity, and PSNR (keeping peak 255) comes out 20 log10(255/219) = 1.321 dB lower. The TID2013 author values psnr.txt ("luminance component") and ssim.txt matched to 4 digits under this convention (10 pairs, 2026-10-04; with full range PSNR is off by −1.3 dB and SSIM by up to 0.05, and without rounding PSNR is off by +0.002-0.07 dB). Neither the page nor the readme says which luminance; this convention was identified by measurement. Rounding is np.round (half to even). For pixels whose luminance falls exactly on k.5, the rounding direction changes with the order of arithmetic and can differ from the author by 1 LSB (in TID2013, 28 pixels of reference I12; for 5 saturation-change pairs the author = perfect match, here 86.6 dB; neither round-half-up nor float32 makes them agree). This only concerns the region where PSNR exceeds 60 dB; the other 2,995 pairs are within 0.0005 dB. Raises ValueError: shape is not (H, W, 3), dtype is not uint8.
